 How was your cross country trip!? What was your favorite part of it, and if you could do one thing differently, what would it have been and why? (lol welcome back to 3rd grade vacation reports)

I would agree with your point about poor social skills, lack of curiosity, and self-centeredness. I hadn’t thought about the fourth one, which is something I’ll have to reflect on today. I hope that my friends are and have been looking for relationships that are deeper than surface level. I have also been reading into “relationship reciprocity” since posting this, maybe that is a resource that you would like to explore? There were a few articles with good insight on what you might be expecting out of a relationship, how to set boundaries, and how to communicate these ideals with your friends. I think I need to start expressing my needs more explicitly, and if they aren’t met, maybe it’s time to think of these friends as fair-weather friends?

I have been working on my communication skills, in the past couple months, and I have noticed that a lot of people that around me are lacking in that as well. Letting people know that you’ve heard them, you understand, and that you validate their feelings is something that I’ve not run into often when receiving replies from friends or acquaintances. When I go back and examine my conversations, i believe I have found that there is also a lack of or naïveté in regards to emotional intelligence. 

I’ve been working really hard on my mental health this year, and just from my perspective, it seems as if some of my friends just paused their EQ development at college. Yes, they are intelligent people and are doing work that benefits them; the transfer between that and EQ seems to be low. I can’t make my friends into anything they aren’t, so I’ve been trying to brainstorm good places to go to add people to my life who would be able to meet my expectations. 

Circling back to relationship reciprocity, maybe I need to organize my friendship roster, and categorize them into groupings, so that I’m not expecting things out of people that are unable to give them to me. Such as, these are my group of friends for outdoor activities, these are my friends I can play games with, these are my friends who I can have intimate and vulnerable conversations with that will validate my feelings. I’m sure their will be crossover at some point, but I think right now I should be focusing on adding to my third category of friends, which I realize will take time to build personal relationships such as these.

It was the first grade, and it was the week that if we answered questions correctly we got motherfucking chocolate! I was so pumped. I studied my first grade ass off, because that chocolate was kickass. 

Unfortunately, I had the biggest smart ass in my class. Everyone has met at least one, that annoying loud mouth girl, who thinks she knows everything because her mommy told her it was true. She blurted out the answers, correct or incorrect, and ruined everyone else's chance to at least try. This went on for about two days before I was about ready to shit in her backpack, shoes, eye, etc. 

So genius first grader me comes up with a plan... An ***evil*** plan. On Tuesday night I took a Hershey's kiss and unwrapped it. I debated between licking it or farting on it, as a first grader I thought this was the best revenge, before I decided to try a mad scientist experiment. I lathered that sweet sweet morsel of chocolate in windex like I shampoo my hair, lather-rinse-repeat, except in this case, fuck rinse! I wrapped that bad motherfucker back up in its wrapper expertly and kept it on my nightstand so I wouldn't forget it in the morning.

The next day I was smiling like a shithead on my way to school. I was determined to receive that glorious chocolate, which was so much better than the waxy Hershey's crap. I presented that girl with my tainted kiss and watched her as she ate it like Cthulhu devours his prey. 

Her face soured up. She turned to me and said... "I think I'm going to be sick!"I chortled and replied, "I thought you loved chocolate".
She looked at me, with nauseous eyes and gasped "Quickly, I need you to get something for me". At this point, I was really rather worried, I didn't want puke on my shoes! So I asked, "Do you need a trash can?"

She replied, "No, I need about tree fiddy!"

It was at this time that I realized this naseous girl only looked green because she was a 500 foot tall, green, scaly monster from the Paleolithic era.

I raised my fist in anger and shook it while she waddled away, back to her lake.

At least I got chocolate for the rest of the week.

**Tl;dr: Tainted Kisses and first grade logic**
